name: Carlos Ibrahim

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government, and we sell nothing. Your answers are confidential. What does a normal day at work look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43, with a two-year college diploma, and I am still a junior developer on low pay. I fix small faults in a fuel-expense app for a tech company; before this I repaired phones at a counter. I like using AI to try a fix quickly, but I need my lead to catch what I miss, and the mortgage plus two school-age children make a failed week expensive.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team our fuel-expense app still needs us to check what a driver actually entered, even if AI tidies a form. I use AI every day to draft small fixes, then ask my lead to check where I have missed something.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The truth is that I’m still a junior on low pay at 43, and we have less than a month of bills saved. My partner Amina’s care shifts change each week; the mortgage feels tight even if AI mostly fizzles.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep working through the fuel-receipt bugs and ask my lead to show me one real mistake in each review. This month we’d cancel the extra television package and put the 25 monthly saving toward the mortgage while our wages continue.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel anxious already. The software job is a chance for me, but I cannot make a missed mortgage payment disappear by coding faster.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did you do before this job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I repaired phones at a small counter, then finished a two-year college diploma and moved into software. I fix screens whether they are cracked or full of code.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who checks the household account?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Amina and I look at the account on Sunday evenings after her rota arrives. The mortgage takes most of our account balance one week each month.

I use **AI daily**, but ask my lead to review my small fixes.
think: I am a **low-paid junior** with less than one month saved.
I worry Amina’s **changing care shifts** leave our mortgage exposed.
do: **Keep fixing** fuel-receipt bugs and ask my lead for one review lesson each week.
**Cancel extra television** and put 25 monthly toward the mortgage while wages continue.
feel: **Anxious already** about the mortgage and changing shifts.
S0.quote: I fix screens whether they are cracked or full of code.
fieldNote: His **daily AI use** speeds small fixes, but he still needs lead review.
The household has **thin savings** and changing care shifts before AI causes any major change.

steps.text: Keep fixing fuel-receipt bugs with weekly lead review
Cancel the extra television package and put 25 monthly toward the mortgage

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell coworkers to measure what AI takes from the junior ticket queue before anyone calls the rollout a success. I’d bring the numbers to our staff group and ask for paid learning time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It already writes much of the small code I am paid to write, so my hours could go first. I like using it, but I have no cushion for a long gap, and Amina cannot take extra care shifts on demand.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d learn a new AI way to trace a fuel receipt from upload to final total, using fake records this month. In the first year I’d take the staff group a count of junior tickets lost and ask for paid training time; I’d also check paid device-repair jobs nearby if my hours are cut.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be alarmed, not surprised. I can learn a new tool quickly, but I cannot hire myself back after a cut.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would your ticket count show?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d note how many receipt fixes a person does each week and how many the tool completes after a check. If the company says nobody loses work, I want those figures beside the promise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you repair phones again?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: There are a few shops, though I do not know if any are hiring. I would apply only to paid openings that fit around the children’s school hours.

I would ask our **staff group** for paid learning time.
think: I expect my **small coding tasks** and hours could go first.
I know Amina cannot add **care shifts** quickly enough to cover a gap.
do: **Learn AI receipt tracing** on fake fuel records this month.
**Bring ticket counts** to the staff group and request paid learning time.
**Check paid repair openings** only if developer hours are cut and vacancies fit the children’s school hours.
feel: **Alarmed** about lost hours despite quick learning.
S1.quote: I can learn a new tool quickly, but I cannot hire myself back after a cut.
fieldNote: He is an **eager daily AI user** who still sees his junior task queue shrinking.
His old **phone-repair skill** offers a conditional job search, not a guaranteed fallback.

steps.text: Learn AI tracing of fuel receipts using fake records

Check paid phone-repair openings fitting children’s school hours if developer hours are cut

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say full AGI by 2028 could do the thinking part of my job, including the fixes I am proud of. Robots around 2031 might later reach hands-on repair, so even my old trade has a date on it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my developer job would end before we have one month of bills saved. Phone repair might bring money for three years before robots get better, but I cannot call it a safe career or count on customers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask the staff group now for written notice and any severance terms, then tell Amina we should call the lender before missing a payment if my pay stops. If AGI arrives in 2028 and I lose the developer role, I’d ask two local repair counters about paid openings and take small phone repairs only when someone pays a deposit for parts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be alarmed and moving fast. I would keep a repair kit by the kitchen door, but it would not cover the whole mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What do you tell the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell our daughter and son that we are holding off on the school trip until we know what I earn. I would not tell them robots are taking their father’s job before we know what the company actually does.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Where does the first repair customer come from?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask former counter customers who still have my number, but I would buy no parts without a deposit. A paid repair could cover groceries, not replace my developer wage.

say: I say **full AGI by 2028** reaches my coding and checking.
I see **repair robots around 2031** as a later threat to my old trade.
think: I expect my **developer wage** could end before we save one month.
I see **phone repair** as temporary money, not a secure replacement.
do: **Seek written notice** through the staff group now.
**Call the lender** before a missed payment if my developer pay stops.
**Ask repair counters** about paid jobs and take deposit-backed repairs if displaced after 2028.
feel: **Alarmed and moving** despite a thin repair income plan.
S2.quote: A paid repair could cover groceries, not replace my developer wage.
fieldNote: He connects the **2028 thinking shock** to coding and the later robot date to hands-on repair.
The repair kit is a **limited bridge**, with deposits required before buying parts.

steps.text: Ask the staff group for written notice and severance terms
Call the mortgage lender before missing a payment if developer pay stops
Ask local repair counters about paid vacancies after displacement

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell our team five years before full AGI in 2031 is enough to show juniors real incidents, not just push out code faster. Robots around 2034 give hands-on repair more time, but the app work changes earlier.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could become better at spotting why a fuel total is wrong, yet AI in 2031 may do even that. I need a second source of pay before then because the mortgage will not pause for a software course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask my lead for one customer fuel-error case each month and write down the cause and fix. I’d start taking paid weekend phone repairs only if customers cover parts up front and Amina can cover childcare; after 2031 I’d apply for paid field-device support openings only if my developer role ends and posts exist.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel anxious, with a job plan I can test slowly. I would still be counting school meals and mortgage dates while I tested it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How many repairs could you manage?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Maybe two a month without taking Sunday from the children. I would keep phone-repair money for a bill buffer, not buy a shop.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the lead refuses the cases?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d work through past incidents on the safe training server and ask for feedback in normal review time. I cannot pay for a long course or take unpaid leave.

say: I want juniors to learn from **real fuel errors** before 2031.
I know **robots around 2034** may later reach hands-on repair.
think: I might improve at **fault finding**, though AGI could do it too.
I need a **second source of pay** before a mortgage gap.
do: **Study one fuel error** monthly with my lead, or past safe incidents if refused.
**Take deposit-backed repairs** on weekends only if childcare is covered.
**Apply for device support** if displaced after 2031 and paid vacancies exist.
feel: **Anxious** while testing a small second income.
S3.quote: I would keep phone-repair money for a bill buffer, not buy a shop.
fieldNote: His **repair income** requires deposits and childcare, and remains small beside the mortgage.
He treats **2034 robots** as a later risk to repair, without pretending his coding lasts that long.

steps.text: Study one real or safe past fuel-error case each month with review
Take weekend phone repairs only with parts deposits and childcare covered
Apply for paid field-device support if displaced after 2031

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say a decade before full AGI in 2036 gives us time to teach juniors how the fuel app fails in real trucks. I would also say robots around 2039 may reach phone and device repair after the coding change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By then our children would be older, but I do not know when the mortgage ends. A longer runway lets me build a few months of bills from wages and repairs, yet my developer work still faces thinking AI in 2036.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting this year I’d keep using AI to draft fixes and set aside one evening monthly to document a real fuel error with my lead. If deposit-backed paid phone repairs come in and Amina can cover the children, I’d save their net proceeds toward three months of bills; if my developer job ends after 2036, I’d seek paid field-support work only where vacancies remain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel anxious about the mortgage today, but less rushed about the far date. I want time to make the repair income real rather than write a hopeful number in a notebook.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make the repair income real?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Three months of paid jobs, with parts costs written down and no missed shifts at my developer job. I would stop if it kept taking family time without leaving money.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does daily AI use still help by 2036?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It helps me find a starting point today, but it does not make me safe from full AGI. I would use it while I still have a paid job and check every answer against a real fuel receipt.

say: I want juniors to learn **real fuel failures** before full AGI reaches coding in 2036.
I know **robots around 2039** may reach hands-on device repair later.
think: I could build **three months of bills** if wages and repair work continue.
I still face **thinking AI in 2036** while the mortgage may remain.
do: **Keep documenting fuel errors** with my lead while using AI for draft fixes.

**Seek paid field support** only if displaced after 2036 and vacancies remain.
feel: **Anxious now** about the mortgage, though the long deadline gives room.
S4.quote: I want time to make the repair income real rather than write a hopeful number in a notebook.
fieldNote: His decade plan tests **actual net repair income** against parts costs and family time.
He treats daily **AI use** as present help, not a defence against 2036 thinking AI.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my developer pay could stop before we have a month saved. Written notice, a chance at paid field-support work and a lender conversation before arrears would help; small phone repairs might cover groceries for a time.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask whether a second job takes the hours my children need from me. I will count the money after parts and childcare, not just the number of repairs.

headlineQuote: The mortgage takes most of our account balance one week each month.
portrait: Carlos is a **43-year-old junior developer** with a two-year diploma, low pay and under one month saved.
He and Amina carry a **mortgage and two children** while her care shifts change each week.
He uses **AI every day** on a fuel-expense app, yet still needs lead review of small fixes.
He brings prior **phone-repair experience** into a cautious, deposit-backed side income plan.
The **2028 scenario** threatens his developer wage before repairs can replace it.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end his developer income before the family builds one month of savings.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, paid openings, early lender contact and deposit-backed repair customers would help cover essentials.
